problems.problem: A --reason that holds a non-UTF-8 byte makes reject crash with a UnicodeEncodeError traceback. Before the crash it leaves an empty (0-byte) <packet>.attempt-N.rejected.json. _records treats the existence of that file as a rejection, so the attempt now counts as failed and stage allows a re-ask, but no reason, attempt_sha256 or time was recorded. A corrected reject is then refused with 'has no stored valid attempt to reject'. The cause: reject dumps with ensure_ascii=False, and Path.write_text creates the file before the encoding fails. This is the same lone-surrogate class as follow-up 4. It is not a regression, since reject is unchanged in this pass. Reproduction: stage case-0001, collect a valid answer, then run `.venv/bin/python -I -B 23-am1-v4.py reject --out DIR --packet case-0001 --reason $'bad \xff byte'`. The result is exit 1 with a traceback, a 0-byte rejection file, and a re-run of reject refused while stage goes through (seen in scratchpad/fix-v4-2/verify/w4).
problems.fix: In reject, do as collect does: if json.dumps(note, ensure_ascii=False) cannot be encoded as UTF-8, dump with ensure_ascii=True. Also make write_new encode the text before it creates the file, for example path.write_bytes(text.encode('utf-8')) after the encode succeeds, so a failed encode never leaves an empty file.

problems.problem: If the workspace does not exist yet and its parent folder is not writable, stage ends with a PermissionError traceback from ws.mkdir instead of a clean refusal. This happens before the marker, so nothing is written or removed. The fixer's report says an unwritable parent refuses cleanly; that is true only when the workspace already exists. The traceback was there before this pass too. Reproduction: mkdir P; chmod 555 P; stage --out DIR --packet audit-07 --workspace P/newws. The result is a traceback ending 'PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: .../p6/newws' (seen in verify/t3_markers.py).
problems.fix: Wrap the mkdir in try/except OSError and raise SystemExit(f"the workspace {ws} could not be created: {exc.strerror or exc}").
